narrative.overview:
The proposal treats procurement as an operating system recorded in a working control ledger, not as an isolated spreadsheet or a generic applicant profile. Warm paper, warehouse-control ink, safety-orange decisions, ruled cells, and instrument labels make the page feel authored for purchasing work: practical, auditable, and implementation-led.

Editorial Newsreader headlines carry the proposal and evidence; Manrope handles the operational detail. The shipped surface opens with the project-led declaration “A procurement system grounded in operational reality,” paired with an interactive Supplier → RFQ → PO → DC → KPI control sheet. A calmer, shorter type hierarchy now carries that same grammar through compact system cells, evidence registers, a dense dark builder console, phased delivery records, five ruled application-answer disclosures, and a print-safe document mode. Reduced type endpoints, card heights, and section cadence lower the total page height without weakening the ledger identity or evidence sequence.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ledger-paper ground with warehouse-green control ink
Safety orange reserved for decisions, progress, evidence, and conversion
Editorial serif declarations paired with compact sans-serif instrument labels
Ruled matrices and registers instead of detached marketing cards
Interactive controls that remain complete as static content and in print
Responsive reduction that keeps high-value process and console records in two columns on mobile

rules.name: The Decision Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange marks a choice, progress, verified scale, or the next action; it is never a general-purpose decoration.

rules.name: The Ledger Contrast Rule
rules.body: Paper and control-ink fields may alternate to establish chapters, but every field retains the same ruled, auditable visual language.

rules.name: The Editorial-to-Instrument Rule
rules.body: Newsreader makes the argument; Manrope operates the system. Never set long process explanations in the display face or let micro-labels become the primary reading voice.

rules.name: The Register Before Elevation Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with rules, tonal fields, and connected cells before adding shadow; only a discrete working artifact may lift off the ledger.

rules.name: The Functional Radius Rule
rules.body: Curves identify controls, stage nodes, or the project mark; operating records remain square so their shared boundaries stay visible.

rules.name: The Static Truth Rule
rules.body: Interaction may reveal stage detail or reading progress, but all claims, evidence, and delivery commitments must remain understandable without motion and printable without dark-background dependence.

rules.name: The Native Disclosure Rule
rules.body: Application answers use named HTML disclosure elements for one-open-at-a-time behavior; do not replace their native keyboard semantics with a custom accordion script.

dos: Do reserve safety orange for decisions, progress, verified scale, and primary actions.
Do structure related information with shared rules, aligned cells, and visible ownership labels.
Do pair large Newsreader declarations with precise Manrope process detail.
Do keep the Supplier → RFQ → PO → DC → KPI chain as the reusable visual model for procurement flow.
Do preserve the responsive and print transformations so the proposal remains useful in short desktop, mobile, and PDF reviews.
Do keep the visual distinction between verified evidence, proposed system controls, and phased delivery outputs.
Do keep application answers in five ruled native disclosure rows and expand all answer content for print.
donts: Don't replace the ledger matrices with floating rounded SaaS cards or a generic applicant-profile grid.
Don't use orange as passive decoration until its decision-making meaning is diluted.
Don't add shadow to ordinary process cells, evidence rows, or delivery phases.
Don't round every record; square shared boundaries are central to the operating-ledger language.
Don't rely on hover, animation, or the interactive chain to carry information that is absent from the document.
Don't introduce unsupported supplier, savings, negotiation, or procurement-performance claims into visual examples.
Don't convert the application answers into floating FAQ cards or allow multiple named disclosure rows to remain open together.
